messages:
sofia: Quick heads-up — after the 2026-03-16 runtime rollout I'm seeing an increase in p99 latency on attention-heavy requests. Baseline before rollout: p50=28ms p95=72ms p99=110ms. After rollout: p50=32ms p95=85ms p99=142ms :grimace:

matt: Ugh. Any obvious change in kernel choice or batching?

sofia: Initial diff shows we changed the kernel selector thresholds and batching heuristics (max_tokens_per_batch from 2048 -> 1024) and enabled the paged_fallback path for some Flash variants.

raj: Can you paste a short profiler flame? even a few lines helps.

sofia: Pasted sampling from canary (warm machine, repeatable):
```
Top kernels by time:
  flash_v2_forward                42.7%  (was 35.1% before)
  fused_attn_fwd                  18.3%  (was 22.0%)
  kv_cache_copy                   14.6%  (was 8.2%)
  alloc/free synchronization      7.9%   (new)
```
Also seeing many small batches with seq_len around 1200 that are triggering paged paths.
```

nora: That kv_cache_copy jump looks suspicious. Could be we regressed a memcpy since selector switched to paged path and does extra copies.

perf-bot: PERF ALERT - p99 latency +29% on route /chat/stream for model redwood/gpt-open-16k between 1945560000 and 1945678000. Full flamegraph: https://perf.internal/flame/1945678901

matt: Proposed hypothesis: smaller batching (max_tokens_per_batch=1024) increased number of requests hitting paged_fallback which does extra KV copying; combined with kernel selector preferring flash_v2 for mid sizes leading to more kernel switches. Kernel switching + memcpy noise -> tail.

raj: I'll run a local bisect. Quick steps I'm doing:
1) Reproduce on canary with traffic replay (same seed)
2) Toggle batching threshold to 2048 to see revert
3) If revert helps, bisect kernel-selector change commits between rollout and previous deploy

sofia: Repro command I used:
```
./runtime/test_replay --model redwood/gpt-open-16k --trace attention --batch-config max_tokens_per_batch=1024 --seed 42
```
Output snippet:
```
P99: 142.1ms
avg memcpy per request: 1.8MB
kv_cache_hits: 0.87
kv_copy_ops: 312
```

raj: Quick experiment: bumped max_tokens_per_batch back to 2048 on one canary host and replayed. Result: p99 down to 116ms. So batching change is definitely a major factor.

nora: Interesting. Does that mean the paged path is fine but the batching heuristic change created many borderline batches that force expensive kernel transitions?

matt: Exactly. If we have many batches crossing seq_len threshold, we're paying kernel warm costs and extra KV copies. Also noticed the selector has an early-return that can force paged path even when fused_attn would be cheaper for short KV sequences.

sofia: Attaching the selector snippet we rolled out:
```
if (seq_len > 1024 && kv_size > 512KB) return paged_flash;
if (batch_tokens > 100k) return flash_v2;
return fused_attn;
```
This is more aggressive toward paged_flash than before.

matt: Suggested mitigation (fast): revert batching max_tokens_per_batch to 2048 (rollback config) and add a prometheus alarm for kernel_switch_count.

perf-bot: ACTION_CREATED: ticket PERF-1872 created (assign=eng-runtime) - investigate kernel selector + batching heuristics.

raj: I'm continuing bisect: git bisect points to commit 3f2a4e9 which changed both the batch default and the selector rule.

nora: For a durable fix we should: (1) refine selector to check average_seq_in_batch not single seq_len, (2) avoid extra KV copies in paged path (use in-place zero-copy pointers), (3) add tests that replay mixed sequence workloads.

sofia: Temporary mitigation deployed: rolled batch max_tokens_per_batch -> 2048 on all canaries and replicated across 2 AZs. p99 back closer to baseline. Rolling rollback to prod?

matt: +1 for rollback. Open PR for config revert and start a small canary for 30m before full rollout. Also add a guard that disables aggressive paged_flash selection when kv_copy_ops > threshold.

nora: I'll open follow-up PRs to: replace paged path memcpy with pointer swapping when possible, add unit tests for selector boundary cases, and a perf test in CI that asserts p99 doesn't regress >10% on replay.

sofia: Thanks. Action items: raj follow up bisect details into PERF-1872, nora to send PRs, matt to coordinate rollback PR, I'll monitor canary and update thread in 30m. :eyes:
